# Part 3 — Joining structural and annotation descriptions

Everything in Part 1 describes the annotation data on its own terms; everything in Part 2 describes the graph on its own terms. Neither is a baseline the other is checked against. This section places them side by side and reads the relationship, which is where the actual analytical content of this project lives.

```{r}
#| label: setup
# Loaded here (not assumed already in scope) so this file can render
# standalone, reading 01_annotation.qmd and 02_network_structure.qmd's
# saved outputs rather than requiring the combined index.qmd include
# chain. If rendered as part of that chain instead, df and
# centrality_df/node_table are already in scope from the included
# upstream parts, and these loads are redundant but harmless (they
# will just re-read the same values from disk).
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
if (!requireNamespace("ggrepel", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("ggrepel", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
library(ggrepel)

# Standard Wilson score interval on a proportion, base R only (matches
# the method underlying stats::prop.test, computed directly here for
# clarity). Used throughout this document as the single, consistent
# criterion for "is a cluster's coverage of a category meaningfully
# above the corpus baseline" — the lower bound of the interval must
# exceed the corpus rate. Replaces earlier, separately-chosen fixed
# floors (an arbitrary minimum count and enrichment ratio) that were
# used in different places in this document without being reconciled
# with each other; one method, defined once, used everywhere below.
wilson_lower_bound <- function(x, n, conf = 0.95) {
  z <- qnorm(1 - (1 - conf) / 2)
  phat <- x / n
  denom <- 1 + z^2 / n
  centre <- phat + z^2 / (2 * n)
  adj <- z * sqrt(phat * (1 - phat) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2))
  (centre - adj) / denom
}
```

```{r}
#| label: join
# df (Part 1's annotation dataframe, from 01_annotation.qmd) is keyed by
# citekey; centrality_df / node_table (Part 2's structural data, from
# 02_network_structure.qmd) is keyed by name (citekey). F1-only:
# annotations exist for F1 papers only. F2 works cited by multiple F1
# papers can still be described using the annotation profile of their
# *citer set*, even though the F2 works themselves are not annotated.
# See "per-F2-node citer profiles" below.

if (!exists("df", inherits = FALSE)) {
  df <- read_csv(here("analysis", "bibvik_annotation_df.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  cat("Loaded df from disk:", nrow(df), "rows\n")
} else {
  cat("df already in scope:", nrow(df), "rows\n")
}
if (!exists("node_table", inherits = FALSE)) {
  node_table <- read_csv(here("analysis", "bibvik_node_table.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  cat("Loaded node_table from disk:", nrow(node_table), "rows\n")
} else {
  cat("node_table already in scope:", nrow(node_table), "rows\n")
}
# node_table, not centrality_df, is the object that actually carries
# community_gn: in 02_network_structure.qmd, node_table is built FROM
# centrality_df with the community assignment joined on afterward
# (node_table <- centrality_df |> left_join(...)), so centrality_df
# itself never has community_gn even when it's in scope. Preferring
# centrality_df here (an earlier version of this join checked for it
# first) silently grabbed the wrong, earlier object in the combined
# index.qmd render, where centrality_df exists but lacks the column
# this file needs — always use node_table.
structural_df <- node_table
cat("structural_df:", nrow(structural_df), "rows. is_ghost values:",
    paste(unique(structural_df$is_ghost), collapse = ", "),
    "(class:", class(structural_df$is_ghost), ")\n")

# is_ghost is written as an R logical (TRUE/FALSE) by 02_network_structure.qmd
# internally, but a round-trip through write_csv()/read_csv() serializes
# logicals as the bare words TRUE/FALSE, not the quoted string "false" the
# original in-memory comparison assumed. Compare against both to be safe
# regardless of whether structural_df came from disk (logical after
# read_csv's type inference) or was passed in memory as character "false".
cluster_table_annotated <- structural_df |>
  filter(is_ghost == FALSE | is_ghost == "false") |>
  left_join(df, by = c("name" = "citekey"))

cat("Joined cluster_table_annotated:", nrow(cluster_table_annotated), "rows\n")
cat("Rows with a matching annotation:", sum(!is.na(cluster_table_annotated$publication_year)), "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: cluster-graph-definitions
#| echo: false
# The same two versions of the graph as in Part 2. node_table carries one
# Girvan-Newman column for each: community_gn (Annotated) and
# community_gn_seed_filtered (Annotated, seed filtered).
graph_labels <- c(annotated = "Annotated", seed_filtered = "Annotated, seed filtered")
gn_columns <- c(annotated = "community_gn", seed_filtered = "community_gn_seed_filtered")
has_gn <- function(key) {
  col <- gn_columns[[key]]
  col %in% names(node_table) && any(!is.na(node_table[[col]]))
}
```


## Cluster structure vs. topics, methods, and sources of evidence

```{r}
#| label: cluster-functions
#| echo: false
# Everything below that is computed per graph goes through these functions,
# called once per tab, so the two tabs of a section cannot drift apart.

# Cluster labels from the labelling step. Only the largest clusters of each run are
# labelled, so a cluster without a label is shown by its number alone.
label_runs <- c(annotated = "annotated", seed_filtered = "annotated_no_seed")
cluster_label_lookup <- function(key) {
  path <- here("analysis", "gn_analysis", "results", label_runs[[key]], "labels", "cluster_labels.csv")
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(character())
  read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    transmute(id = as.character(community_id), label = label) |>
    deframe()
}
cluster_names <- function(key, width = 200) {
  lookup <- cluster_label_lookup(key)
  set_names(str_trunc(unname(lookup), width), names(lookup))
}

# The annotated works with a cluster in this graph, and the true size of every cluster.
cluster_context <- function(key) {
  col <- gn_columns[[key]]
  assigned <- cluster_table_annotated |>
    mutate(community_gn = as.character(.data[[col]])) |>
    filter(!is.na(community_gn))
  list(
    annotated_only = filter(assigned, !is.na(publication_year)),
    true_sizes = node_table |>
      filter(!is.na(.data[[col]])) |>
      count(community_gn = as.character(.data[[col]]), name = "true_size"),
    names = cluster_names(key),
    names_long = cluster_names(key)
  )
}

# Coverage and enrichment of one category family (topic, method or source of
# evidence) in the clusters tied for the 20 most annotated works.
category_data <- function(ctx, pattern, kind, unit = "Cluster", unit_names = NULL) {
  long <- ctx$annotated_only |>
    select(name, community_gn, contains(pattern)) |>
    pivot_longer(contains(pattern), names_to = "category", values_to = "value") |>
    filter(!is.na(value)) |>
    mutate(category = str_replace_all(str_remove(category, pattern), fixed("."), " "))
  annotated_n <- long |> distinct(community_gn, name) |> count(community_gn, name = "n_annotated")
  keep <- annotated_n |> slice_max(n_annotated, n = 20) |> pull(community_gn)
  labels <- annotated_n |>
    filter(community_gn %in% keep) |>
    left_join(ctx$true_sizes, by = "community_gn") |>
    arrange(desc(true_size)) |>
    mutate(label = sprintf("%s %s%s (%d of %d annotated)", unit, community_gn,
                           {
                             nm <- if (is.null(unit_names)) rep(NA_character_, n()) else unname(unit_names[community_gn])
                             ifelse(is.na(nm), "", paste0(": ", nm))
                           },
                           n_annotated, true_size)) |>
    mutate(label = fct_rev(fct_inorder(label))) |>
    select(community_gn, label) |>
    deframe()
  # Corpus-wide base rate per category: what fraction of ALL annotated works
  # (not just the 20 shown clusters) carry it. Dividing a cluster's coverage by
  # this rate gives enrichment, the signal of thematic distinctiveness.
  corpus_rate <- long |>
    distinct(name, category) |>
    count(category, name = "n_corpus") |>
    mutate(corpus_rate = n_corpus / n_distinct(long$name))
  enrichment <- long |>
    filter(community_gn %in% keep) |>
    distinct(community_gn, name, category) |>
    count(community_gn, category) |>
    left_join(annotated_n, by = "community_gn") |>
    left_join(corpus_rate, by = "category") |>
    mutate(prop = n / n_annotated, enrichment = prop / corpus_rate,
           ci_lower = wilson_lower_bound(n, n_annotated), category_type = kind)
  list(kind = kind, long = long, annotated_n = annotated_n, keep = keep, labels = labels,
       corpus_rate = corpus_rate, enrichment = enrichment)
}

cluster_data <- map(set_names(names(gn_columns)), function(key) {
  if (!has_gn(key)) return(NULL)
  ctx <- cluster_context(key)
  ctx$topic <- category_data(ctx, "Topics..", "topic", unit_names = ctx$names)
  ctx$method <- category_data(ctx, "Methods..", "method", unit_names = ctx$names)
  ctx$source <- category_data(ctx, "Sources.of.Evidence..", "source", unit_names = ctx$names)
  ctx$n_matched <- nrow(ctx$annotated_only)
  sizes <- arrange(ctx$true_sizes, desc(true_size))
  ctx$n_clusters <- nrow(sizes)
  ctx$size_drop <- sizes$true_size[1] - sizes$true_size[2]
  ctx$n_pass_3plus <- ctx$topic$long |> distinct(community_gn, name) |> count(community_gn) |> filter(n >= 3) |> nrow()
  ctx
})

# How many clusters the heatmaps show (every cluster tied for the 20 most annotated works),
# and the most annotated works any cluster holds.
heatmap_n <- function(key) if (has_gn(key)) length(cluster_data[[key]]$topic$keep) else "n/a"
most_annotated <- function() max(map_dbl(compact(cluster_data), \(d) max(d$topic$annotated_n$n_annotated)))
# Figure height that gives every cluster row room for its label.
heatmap_height <- function(key, kind) {
  n <- if (has_gn(key)) length(cluster_data[[key]][[kind]]$keep) else 0
  max(7, 0.3 * n + 2)
}

category_note <- function(key, kind, data = cluster_data) {
  d <- data[[key]]
  cat("Works with a cluster assignment and any ", kind, " coded: ", n_distinct(d[[kind]]$long$name), "\n\n", sep = "")
}

category_heatmap <- function(key, kind, data = cluster_data, unit = "cluster") {
  d <- data[[key]][[kind]]
  family <- c(topic = "Topic", method = "Method", source = "Source-of-evidence")[[kind]]
  tail_text <- c(
    topic = paste0("a cluster at 1x carries the topic at exactly the corpus average; ubiquitous topics (e.g. Environment) will not dominate every row here the way they do on raw coverage"),
    method = "ubiquitous methods (e.g. Spatial analysis) will not dominate every row here the way they do on raw coverage",
    source = "ubiquitous sources (e.g. Written sources, Graves and monuments) will not dominate every row here the way they do on raw coverage")[[kind]]
  tail_text <- str_replace(tail_text, "a cluster at 1x", paste0("a ", unit, " at 1x"))
  d$enrichment |>
    mutate(cluster_label = d$labels[as.character(community_gn)]) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = category, y = cluster_label, fill = enrichment)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = n), size = 3, colour = "grey20") +
    # Diverging scale centred on 1.0 (cluster rate == corpus rate): blue means
    # this cluster carries the category more than the corpus baseline
    # (distinctive), red means less. Capped at 3x so a handful of extreme
    # small-n ratios don't wash out the rest of the scale.
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "firebrick", mid = "white", high = "steelblue",
                         midpoint = 1, limits = c(0, 3), oob = scales::squish,
                         labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "x")) +
    labs(x = "", y = "", fill = "Enrichment vs.\ncorpus base rate",
         title = paste0(family, " enrichment within each Girvan-Newman ", unit, ", ", graph_labels[[key]]),
         subtitle = (function(s) str_wrap(s, 150))(
           paste0("Cell numbers are raw counts. Fill shows coverage relative to the corpus-wide rate for that ",
                  kind, ", not raw coverage — ", tail_text))) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          plot.title.position = "plot")
}

# A peak requires the Wilson lower bound (defined in setup) on a cluster's
# coverage rate to exceed the corpus baseline rate for that category.
cluster_peaks <- function(key, data = cluster_data) {
  d <- data[[key]]
  bind_rows(d$topic$enrichment, d$method$enrichment, d$source$enrichment) |>
    filter(ci_lower > corpus_rate)
}

cluster_signatures <- function(key) {
  cluster_peaks(key) |>
    group_by(community_gn) |>
    summarise(
      n_peaks = n(),
      mean_peak_enrichment = mean(enrichment),
      peak_categories = paste0(category_type, ": ", category, " (", round(enrichment, 1), "x)", collapse = "; "),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(desc(n_peaks), desc(mean_peak_enrichment))
}

# No composite "score" here. Peak count x mean enrichment is not a real unit and
# a single number invites over-interpretation, so the two are plotted directly.
signature_plot <- function(key) {
  cat("Peaks found (Wilson lower bound exceeds corpus baseline): ", nrow(cluster_peaks(key)), "\n\n", sep = "")
  cluster_signatures(key) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = n_peaks, y = mean_peak_enrichment, label = community_gn)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, colour = "steelblue") +
    geom_text_repel(size = 3.5, seed = 1, max.overlaps = Inf) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty()) +
    labs(x = "Number of peaks (categories where coverage exceeds\ncorpus baseline, Wilson 95% lower bound)",
         y = "Mean enrichment among those peaks",
         title = paste0("Clusters by peak count and peak strength, ", graph_labels[[key]]),
         subtitle = "Upper right: several strong, corroborating signals. Lower right: one very strong but isolated signal.") +
    theme_minimal()
}

signature_detail <- function(key) {
  nm <- cluster_data[[key]]$names_long
  cluster_text <- function(id) paste0("Cluster ", id, ifelse(is.na(nm[id]), "", paste0(": ", nm[id])))
  top_communities <- cluster_signatures(key) |> slice_max(n_peaks, n = 8, with_ties = FALSE) |> pull(community_gn)
  cluster_peaks(key) |>
    filter(community_gn %in% top_communities) |>
    mutate(
      cluster_label = fct_relevel(cluster_text(community_gn), cluster_text(top_communities)),
      category_label = fct_reorder(paste0(category, " (", category_type, ")"), enrichment)
    ) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = enrichment, y = category_label)) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    facet_wrap(vars(cluster_label), scales = "free_y", ncol = 2, labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 60)) +
    labs(x = "Enrichment vs. corpus base rate", y = "",
         title = paste0("Peak categories for the clusters with the most peaks, ", graph_labels[[key]]),
         subtitle = "Dashed line = corpus baseline (1x). Bars are that cluster's individual peaks.") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10))
}

# Tables that sit beside the plots, as extra tabs. Each is built from the
# same objects as its plot, so a table holds exactly the numbers the plot
# draws. Shares are rounded for reading.

# One row per cluster (or group) and category: the numbers behind a heatmap.
# Rows run largest cluster first, as the heatmap's rows do from the top, and
# strongest enrichment first within a cluster. `peak` marks a category whose
# Wilson lower bound exceeds the corpus rate, the criterion used throughout.
category_table <- function(key, kind, data = cluster_data, unit = "Cluster") {
  ctx <- data[[key]]
  ctx[[kind]]$enrichment |>
    left_join(ctx$true_sizes, by = "community_gn") |>
    arrange(desc(true_size), community_gn, desc(enrichment)) |>
    transmute(
      id = community_gn,
      label = unname(ctx$names[community_gn]),
      size = true_size,
      annotated = n_annotated,
      category,
      n,
      share = round(100 * prop, 1),
      corpus_pct = round(100 * corpus_rate, 1),
      enrichment = round(enrichment, 2),
      wilson_lower = round(100 * ci_lower, 1),
      peak = if_else(ci_lower > corpus_rate, "peak", "")
    ) |>
    set_names(c(unit, "label", paste(tolower(unit), "size"), "annotated works", "category",
                "works with it", "share (%)", "corpus rate (%)", "enrichment",
                "Wilson 95% lower bound (%)", "peak"))
}

# The data behind the peak count against peak strength plot.
signature_table <- function(key) {
  nm <- cluster_data[[key]]$names_long
  cluster_signatures(key) |>
    transmute(Cluster = community_gn, label = unname(nm[community_gn]),
              peaks = n_peaks, `mean enrichment` = round(mean_peak_enrichment, 2),
              `peak categories (enrichment)` = peak_categories)
}

# The data behind the peak categories plot: the same eight clusters, in the
# plot's order.
signature_detail_table <- function(key) {
  nm <- cluster_data[[key]]$names_long
  top_communities <- cluster_signatures(key) |> slice_max(n_peaks, n = 8, with_ties = FALSE) |> pull(community_gn)
  cluster_peaks(key) |>
    filter(community_gn %in% top_communities) |>
    mutate(cluster_order = match(community_gn, top_communities)) |>
    arrange(cluster_order, desc(enrichment)) |>
    transmute(Cluster = community_gn, label = unname(nm[community_gn]), category,
              type = category_type, `works with it` = n, `annotated works` = n_annotated,
              `share (%)` = round(100 * prop, 1), `corpus rate (%)` = round(100 * corpus_rate, 1),
              enrichment = round(enrichment, 2),
              `Wilson 95% lower bound (%)` = round(100 * ci_lower, 1))
}
```


`community_gn` (Girvan-Newman, fragmentation-onset cut) is checked here
against the topics, methods, and sources of evidence coded in Part 1,
for both versions of the graph. Annotated uses the cut of the Annotated
run and Annotated, seed filtered uses the cut of the seed-filtered run.
The comparison is restricted to works with a matching annotation
(F1-only; see the join above), which is
`r if (has_gn("annotated")) cluster_data$annotated$n_matched else "n/a"`
works in Annotated and
`r if (has_gn("seed_filtered")) cluster_data$seed_filtered$n_matched else "n/a"`
in Annotated, seed filtered. Louvain and Leiden cluster assignments also
exist from Part 2 but are not used in this section.

Coverage is thin relative to the graph as a whole: in Annotated,
`r if (has_gn("annotated")) cluster_data$annotated$n_matched else "n/a"` annotated
works out of `r nrow(node_table)` nodes, and within any single cluster
that annotated count is often a small fraction of the cluster's real
size (the heatmaps below show the clusters tied for the 20 most annotated
works, `r heatmap_n("annotated")` in Annotated and `r heatmap_n("seed_filtered")` in Annotated, seed filtered, and no
cluster holds more than `r most_annotated()` annotated works out of a much larger
true membership). A prior
exploratory pass on an earlier GN cut of this same corpus found 7-13
annotated nodes per cluster typical, out of hundreds of members, and
treated agreement between structure and annotation as directionally
suggestive rather than comprehensively verified for that reason. The
same caution applies here: what follows can show that structure and
coding line up somewhere, but cannot rule out that the uncoded majority
of any cluster tells a different story.

The coded columns are wide, one column per topic/method/source
category, valued `"Primary"`, `"Secondary"`, or blank. Primary and
secondary are merged throughout what follows: a work counts as coded
with a category at either level, matching the method used in a prior
exploratory pass on an earlier GN cut of this corpus. A work can carry
more than one topic, method, or source, so per-cluster percentages
below do not sum to 100%; each cell shows the raw count behind its
percentage for transparency.

**How to read the enrichment heatmaps below.** Raw coverage (what
fraction of a cluster's annotated works carry a given category) is
misleading on its own: some categories are common across the whole
corpus regardless of cluster — "Spatial analysis" as a method, or
"Environment" as a topic, show up in most clusters simply because
most works in this corpus use them, not because any one cluster is
distinctively characterized by them. To separate genuine
distinctiveness from corpus-wide popularity, each heatmap cell instead
shows **enrichment**: a cluster's coverage of a category divided by
that category's rate across the whole annotated corpus. A value of 1x
means the cluster carries the category at exactly the corpus
average; 2x means twice the corpus rate; 0.5x means half. White is 1x
(baseline); blue is above baseline (the category is over-represented in
that cluster, a real distinguishing signal); red is below baseline
(under-represented). For example, if "Palaeoenvironment reconstruction"
is coded in 23% of the whole corpus but 100% of a given cluster's
annotated works, that cell shows roughly 4.4x — a real signal that
environmental method is disproportionately concentrated there, not
just present because it's common everywhere.

### By topic

**Girvan-Newman clusters by topic.** A threshold of 3+ annotated
works lets through only a small share of the clusters in this corpus (see
the counts below), so it does not give a workable set. Shown here
instead, in the heatmap below: the clusters tied for the 20 most annotated works
(`r heatmap_n("annotated")` in Annotated and `r heatmap_n("seed_filtered")` in Annotated, seed filtered, because many
clusters tie at two annotated works). This is a readability choice, not a derived breakpoint.

At this cut, Annotated has
`r if (has_gn("annotated")) format(cluster_data$annotated$n_clusters, big.mark = ",") else "n/a"` clusters,
`r if (has_gn("annotated")) cluster_data$annotated$n_pass_3plus else "n/a"` of which pass a
3+ annotated-works threshold, and its largest cluster is
`r if (has_gn("annotated")) cluster_data$annotated$size_drop else "n/a"` members larger than
the second-largest. Annotated, seed filtered has
`r if (has_gn("seed_filtered")) format(cluster_data$seed_filtered$n_clusters, big.mark = ",") else "n/a"` clusters,
`r if (has_gn("seed_filtered")) cluster_data$seed_filtered$n_pass_3plus else "n/a"` of which pass
the threshold, and its largest cluster is
`r if (has_gn("seed_filtered")) cluster_data$seed_filtered$size_drop else "n/a"` members larger than
the second-largest.

Coverage varies a lot by cluster (annotation is thin relative to true
cluster size, per the caveat above), so each row label shows how many
annotated works its percentages are based on, out of the cluster's
true total size.

## Cluster signatures: peak count and peak strength

Throughout this section, "cluster" means a Girvan-Newman graph
cluster (`community_gn`), not a scholarly or social cluster.

The topic, method, and source enrichment findings above surface
individual standout cells one at a time. This section combines them
into two directly interpretable numbers per cluster, so the
clusters most worth a closer look surface first instead of
requiring a manual scan across three separate tables.

A **peak** is any category (topic, method, or source) whose 95% Wilson
confidence interval on a cluster's coverage rate lies entirely above
the corpus-wide rate for that category — meaning the cluster's
coverage is higher than baseline with reasonable statistical
confidence, not just a higher raw count. This adapts to sample size
automatically: a cluster with only 3 annotated works needs a much
larger raw enrichment to register as a peak than a cluster with 13,
because a small sample's interval is wider. This is the same criterion
used in the topic, method, and source findings above (`ci_lower >
corpus_rate`); "peak" here just names a category that already met that
bar, so this section's peak count and mean enrichment are computed
directly from the same standouts listed there, not a separate pass.

For each cluster, two numbers: how many peaks it has, and how strong
those peaks are on average. Neither is combined into a single score —
peak count times mean enrichment is not a real, interpretable unit, and
collapsing two different kinds of signal into one number invites
over-reading it. Plotted directly instead: clusters with many peaks
AND high average enrichment are worth reading first; a cluster with
one very large but isolated peak is a different kind of finding (a
strong single signal) than one with several moderate peaks (a broader,
possibly more coherent pattern) — the plot keeps that distinction
visible rather than flattening it. Whether a cluster's peak
categories actually cohere thematically is a judgment that requires
reading them against domain knowledge of this corpus, which this plot
does not attempt.

## Groups of clusters vs. topics, methods, and sources of evidence

```{r}
#| label: group-functions
#| echo: false
# Part 2 sorts the Girvan-Newman clusters into groups by consensus. Only groups of two or
# more clusters are used here, as in Part 2, and each is named for its largest cluster.
# category_data() and the heatmap function above are reused, with the group number
# carried in the same id column the clusters use.
group_columns <- c(annotated = "group_gn", seed_filtered = "group_gn_seed_filtered")
has_groups <- function(key) {
  col <- group_columns[[key]]
  has_gn(key) && col %in% names(node_table) && any(!is.na(node_table[[col]]))
}

# Groups with fewer annotated works than this are listed but not tested: the Wilson interval
# cannot tell a pattern from chance in a handful of papers, and one paper is enough to make
# any rare category look like a peak.
group_min_annotated <- 10

group_context <- function(key) {
  gcol <- group_columns[[key]]
  ccol <- gn_columns[[key]]
  lookup <- cluster_label_lookup(key)
  groups <- node_table |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[gcol]]), !is.na(.data[[ccol]])) |>
    count(group = .data[[gcol]], cluster = .data[[ccol]], name = "papers") |>
    group_by(group) |>
    summarise(lead = cluster[which.max(papers)], n_clusters = n(), true_size = sum(papers), .groups = "drop") |>
    filter(n_clusters >= 2) |>
    mutate(name = coalesce(unname(lookup[as.character(lead)]), paste("Community", lead)))
  annotated_all <- cluster_table_annotated |>
    mutate(community_gn = as.character(.data[[gcol]])) |>
    filter(community_gn %in% as.character(groups$group), !is.na(publication_year))
  per_group <- count(annotated_all, community_gn, name = "n_annotated")
  eligible <- per_group$community_gn[per_group$n_annotated >= group_min_annotated]
  list(
    annotated_only = filter(annotated_all, community_gn %in% eligible),
    true_sizes = transmute(groups, community_gn = as.character(group), true_size = true_size),
    names = set_names(groups$name, as.character(groups$group)),
    groups = groups,
    per_group = per_group,
    eligible = eligible
  )
}

group_data <- map(set_names(names(gn_columns)), function(key) {
  if (!has_groups(key)) return(NULL)
  ctx <- group_context(key)
  ctx$topic <- category_data(ctx, "Topics..", "topic", "Group", ctx$names)
  ctx$method <- category_data(ctx, "Methods..", "method", "Group", ctx$names)
  ctx$source <- category_data(ctx, "Sources.of.Evidence..", "source", "Group", ctx$names)
  ctx$n_matched <- nrow(ctx$annotated_only)
  ctx$n_categories <- nrow(ctx$topic$corpus_rate) + nrow(ctx$method$corpus_rate) + nrow(ctx$source$corpus_rate)
  ctx$peaks <- cluster_peaks(key, set_names(list(ctx), key))
  ctx
})

# One row per group: its size, its annotated works, and the strongest categories it carries
# above the corpus rate (Wilson lower bound, as for the clusters).
group_peak_table <- function(key) {
  d <- group_data[[key]]
  strongest <- d$peaks |>
    group_by(community_gn) |>
    arrange(desc(enrichment), .by_group = TRUE) |>
    summarise(
      n_peaks = n(),
      strongest = paste0(head(paste0(category, " (", round(enrichment, 1), "x, ", n, " of ", n_annotated, ")"), 3), collapse = "; "),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  d$groups |>
    mutate(community_gn = as.character(group)) |>
    left_join(d$per_group, by = "community_gn") |>
    left_join(strongest, by = "community_gn") |>
    arrange(group) |>
    transmute(
      Group = paste0(group, ". ", name),
      Clusters = n_clusters,
      Papers = format(true_size, big.mark = ","),
      `Annotated papers` = coalesce(n_annotated, 0L),
      Peaks = if_else(community_gn %in% d$eligible, as.character(coalesce(n_peaks, 0L)), "not tested"),
      `Strongest peaks (enrichment, annotated papers with it of those coded)` =
        if_else(community_gn %in% d$eligible, coalesce(strongest, "none"), paste0("fewer than ", group_min_annotated, " annotated works"))
    ) |>
    knitr::kable()
}

group_summary_text <- function() {
  one <- function(key) {
    if (!has_groups(key)) return("n/a")
    d <- group_data[[key]]
    tested <- filter(d$per_group, community_gn %in% d$eligible)
    with_peak <- n_distinct(d$peaks$community_gn)
    top <- d$peaks |> slice_max(enrichment, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
    paste0(nrow(d$groups), " groups, of which ", nrow(tested), " hold at least ", group_min_annotated, " annotated works (between ",
           min(tested$n_annotated), " and ", max(tested$n_annotated), " each); ", with_peak, " of those ", nrow(tested),
           " carry at least one peak (", nrow(d$peaks), " peaks in all), and the strongest is ", top$category, " in Group ",
           top$community_gn, " at ", round(top$enrichment, 1), "x")
  }
  paste0("In Annotated there are ", one("annotated"), ". In Annotated, seed filtered there are ", one("seed_filtered"), ".")
}
```

Part 2 sorts the Girvan-Newman clusters into groups, using a consensus of eight community-detection variants run with five seeds each. This section repeats the comparison above one level up: each group's annotated works are compared with the annotation of the whole corpus. Enrichment, peaks and heatmaps work as described above, with a group in place of a cluster. `r group_summary_text()` Groups with fewer than `r group_min_annotated` annotated works are listed in the first table but left out of the peaks and heatmaps. Each remaining group holds a few dozen annotated works at most, so only large gaps register as peaks. Each is compared on `r group_data$annotated$n_categories` categories, and about one peak per group could arise by chance at this bound. The uncoded majority of each group may tell a different story.

## Hubs of Shared references and Single hub clusters

```{r}
#| label: hub-functions
#| echo: false
# The hubs of Shared references clusters beside the hubs of Single hub clusters.
# Part 2 writes each paper's cluster shape and whether it is a hub of its cluster
# into the node table. A hub here is a paper that cites other members of its cluster.
hub_shape_columns <- c(annotated = "shape_gn", seed_filtered = "shape_gn_seed_filtered")
hub_flag_columns <- c(annotated = "cluster_hub_gn", seed_filtered = "cluster_hub_gn_seed_filtered")
hub_groups <- c("Shared references", "Single hub")
hub_colours <- c("Shared references" = "firebrick", "Single hub" = "steelblue")
hub_families <- c("Topic", "Method", "Source of evidence")

has_hubs <- function(key) {
  all(c(hub_shape_columns[[key]], hub_flag_columns[[key]]) %in% names(node_table)) &&
    any(!is.na(node_table[[hub_shape_columns[[key]]]]))
}

# Wilson score interval (the same method as wilson_lower_bound), both bounds.
wilson_bounds <- function(x, n, conf = 0.95) {
  z <- qnorm(1 - (1 - conf) / 2)
  phat <- x / n
  denom <- 1 + z^2 / n
  centre <- phat + z^2 / (2 * n)
  adj <- z * sqrt(phat * (1 - phat) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2))
  tibble(lower = (centre - adj) / denom, upper = (centre + adj) / denom)
}

# The annotated hubs of the two shapes, one row per hub, with every category column.
hub_papers <- function(key) {
  cluster_table_annotated |>
    filter(as.logical(.data[[hub_flag_columns[[key]]]]) %in% TRUE,
           .data[[hub_shape_columns[[key]]]] %in% hub_groups,
           !is.na(publication_year)) |>
    transmute(name, shape = .data[[hub_shape_columns[[key]]]],
              across(c(contains("Topics.."), contains("Methods.."), contains("Sources.of.Evidence.."))))
}

# One row per category and group: the hubs that carry it, their share of the group, and
# the Wilson interval on that share. A hub carries a category when the column has a value.
hub_cells <- function(key) {
  hubs <- hub_papers(key)
  sizes <- count(hubs, shape, name = "hubs")
  cells <- hubs |>
    pivot_longer(-c(name, shape), names_to = "column", values_to = "value") |>
    mutate(family = case_when(str_detect(column, fixed("Topics..")) ~ "Topic",
                              str_detect(column, fixed("Methods..")) ~ "Method",
                              TRUE ~ "Source of evidence"),
           category = str_squish(str_replace_all(
             str_remove(column, "^(Topics|Methods|Sources\\.of\\.Evidence)\\.\\."), fixed("."), " "))) |>
    group_by(family, category, shape) |>
    summarise(n = sum(!is.na(value)), .groups = "drop") |>
    left_join(sizes, by = "shape") |>
    mutate(share = n / hubs)
  bind_cols(cells, wilson_bounds(cells$n, cells$hubs))
}

# Shared references against Single hub for every category. The interval on the
# difference is built from the two Wilson intervals (Newcombe's method), and a
# category differs when that interval excludes zero.
hub_comparison <- function(key) {
  cells <- hub_cells(key)
  inner_join(filter(cells, shape == "Shared references"), filter(cells, shape == "Single hub"),
             by = c("family", "category"), suffix = c("_shared", "_single")) |>
    mutate(difference = share_shared - share_single,
           diff_lower = difference - sqrt((share_shared - lower_shared)^2 + (upper_single - share_single)^2),
           diff_upper = difference + sqrt((upper_shared - share_shared)^2 + (share_single - lower_single)^2),
           differs = diff_lower > 0 | diff_upper < 0,
           family = factor(family, levels = hub_families)) |>
    arrange(family, desc(difference), category)
}

hub_note <- function(key) {
  d <- hub_comparison(key)
  sizes <- d |> slice(1) |> transmute(a = hubs_shared, b = hubs_single)
  flagged <- d |> filter(differs) |> arrange(desc(abs(difference)))
  paste0("The comparison covers ", sizes$a, " annotated hubs in Shared references clusters and ", sizes$b,
         " in Single hub clusters. ", nrow(flagged), " of ", nrow(d), " categories differ",
         if (nrow(flagged) > 0) paste0(": ", paste0(flagged$category, " (", sprintf("%+.0f", 100 * flagged$difference), " points)", collapse = ", ")) else "",
         ".")
}

hub_plot <- function(key) {
  d <- hub_comparison(key) |>
    mutate(label = if_else(differs, paste0(category, " *"), category),
           row = fct_rev(fct_inorder(paste(family, category, sep = "||"))))
  long <- bind_rows(
    transmute(d, family, row, label, group = "Shared references", share = share_shared, lower = lower_shared, upper = upper_shared),
    transmute(d, family, row, label, group = "Single hub", share = share_single, lower = lower_single, upper = upper_single))
  lookup <- distinct(d, row, label) |> deframe()
  ggplot(long, aes(share, row, colour = group)) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), size = 0.3) +
    facet_grid(family ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = hub_colours, name = NULL, breaks = hub_groups) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = lookup) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "Share of the group's annotated hubs", y = NULL,
         title = paste0(graph_labels[[key]], ": categories carried by the hubs of Shared references and Single hub clusters"),
         subtitle = "Points are shares with Wilson 95% intervals. A star marks a difference whose 95% interval excludes zero.") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))
}

hub_table <- function(key) {
  as_interval <- function(lower, upper) paste0(round(100 * lower, 1), " to ", round(100 * upper, 1))
  hub_comparison(key) |>
    transmute(Kind = as.character(family), Category = category,
              `Hubs, Shared references` = n_shared, `Share (%), Shared references` = round(100 * share_shared, 1),
              `Interval (%), Shared references` = as_interval(lower_shared, upper_shared),
              `Hubs, Single hub` = n_single, `Share (%), Single hub` = round(100 * share_single, 1),
              `Interval (%), Single hub` = as_interval(lower_single, upper_single),
              `Difference (points)` = round(100 * difference, 1),
              `Difference interval (points)` = as_interval(diff_lower, diff_upper),
              `Interval excludes zero` = if_else(differs, "yes", "no")) |>
    knitr::kable()
}
```

A hub is a paper that cites other members of its cluster, and Part 2 sorts every cluster into a shape by how its hubs cite. This section sets the annotated hubs of Shared references clusters beside the annotated hubs of Single hub clusters, to see whether the two kinds of cluster draw on different topics, methods and sources of evidence. A hub carries a category when the annotation marks it as primary or secondary. Each point is the share of a group's hubs that carry a category, with its Wilson 95% interval. The difference between the two shares has an interval built from the two Wilson intervals (Newcombe's method), and a category counts as different when that interval excludes zero. The intervals are not adjusted for the number of categories compared, and the Shared references group is small.

## Self-citation by topic, method and source of evidence

```{r}
#| label: selfcat-functions
#| echo: false
# Self-citation of the annotated papers that carry a category beside the papers that do
# not. Part 2 writes each annotated paper's citations to works with a known author list,
# and how many of them are self-citations, into the node table. A paper carries a
# category when the annotation marks it as primary or secondary.
selfcat_families <- c("Topic", "Method", "Source of evidence")
selfcat_reps <- 2000

has_self <- function() {
  all(c("citations_known_authors", "self_citations_any_author", "self_citations_first_author") %in% names(node_table)) &&
    any(!is.na(node_table$citations_known_authors))
}

# Runs `code` with a fixed random seed and puts the random number state back afterwards.
with_fixed_seed <- function(seed, code) {
  old <- if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())) get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  on.exit(if (is.null(old)) rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()) else assign(".Random.seed", old, envir = globalenv()))
  set.seed(seed)
  code
}

# One row per annotated paper with citations, and a 0/1 matrix of the categories it carries.
selfcat_data <- function() {
  papers <- cluster_table_annotated |>
    filter(!is.na(publication_year), !is.na(citations_known_authors)) |>
    select(name, citations = citations_known_authors, any_author = self_citations_any_author,
           first_author = self_citations_first_author,
           contains("Topics.."), contains("Methods.."), contains("Sources.of.Evidence.."))
  cats <- tibble(column = setdiff(names(papers), c("name", "citations", "any_author", "first_author"))) |>
    mutate(family = case_when(str_detect(column, fixed("Topics..")) ~ "Topic",
                              str_detect(column, fixed("Methods..")) ~ "Method",
                              TRUE ~ "Source of evidence"),
           category = str_squish(str_replace_all(
             str_remove(column, "^(Topics|Methods|Sources\\.of\\.Evidence)\\.\\."), fixed("."), " ")))
  list(papers = papers, cats = cats, carry = 1 * as.matrix(!is.na(papers[cats$column])))
}

# For every category: the share of citations that are self-citations among the papers that
# carry it and among the papers that do not, and the difference. A share is the group's
# self-citations over the group's citations, so a paper with a long reference list weighs
# more. The interval on the difference comes from resampling the papers, because the
# citations of one paper are not independent of each other.
selfcat_comparison <- function() {
  d <- selfcat_data()
  n <- nrow(d$papers)
  weights <- with_fixed_seed(1, replicate(selfcat_reps, tabulate(sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE), nbins = n)))
  measure <- function(events) {
    carry_events <- colSums(d$carry * events)
    carry_citations <- colSums(d$carry * d$papers$citations)
    point <- carry_events / carry_citations - (sum(events) - carry_events) / (sum(d$papers$citations) - carry_citations)
    boot_events <- crossprod(weights * events, d$carry)
    boot_citations <- crossprod(weights * d$papers$citations, d$carry)
    boot <- boot_events / boot_citations -
      (colSums(weights * events) - boot_events) / (colSums(weights * d$papers$citations) - boot_citations)
    bounds <- apply(boot, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)
    tibble(carrying = 100 * carry_events / carry_citations,
           not_carrying = 100 * (sum(events) - carry_events) / (sum(d$papers$citations) - carry_citations),
           difference = 100 * point, lower = 100 * bounds[1, ], upper = 100 * bounds[2, ],
           excludes_zero = bounds[1, ] > 0 | bounds[2, ] < 0)
  }
  first <- measure(d$papers$first_author)
  any <- measure(d$papers$any_author)
  bind_cols(select(d$cats, family, category), papers = colSums(d$carry),
            rename_with(first, ~ paste0("first_", .x)), rename_with(any, ~ paste0("any_", .x))) |>
    mutate(family = factor(family, levels = selfcat_families)) |>
    arrange(family, desc(first_difference), category)
}

selfcat_note <- function() {
  d <- selfcat_comparison()
  p <- selfcat_data()$papers
  flagged <- function(prefix) {
    f <- d[d[[paste0(prefix, "_excludes_zero")]], ]
    f <- f[order(-abs(f[[paste0(prefix, "_difference")]])), ]
    shown <- head(f, 5)
    paste0(nrow(f), " of ", nrow(d), " categories",
           if (nrow(f) > 0) paste0(" (", paste0(shown$category, " ", sprintf("%+.1f", shown[[paste0(prefix, "_difference")]]), collapse = ", "),
                                   if (nrow(f) > 5) paste0(", and ", nrow(f) - 5, " more") else "", ")") else "")
  }
  paste0("Across the ", nrow(p), " annotated papers, ", scales::percent(sum(p$first_author) / sum(p$citations), accuracy = 0.1),
         " of citations go to a work by the citing paper's first author and ",
         scales::percent(sum(p$any_author) / sum(p$citations), accuracy = 0.1), " to a work that shares an author with it. ",
         "The first-author rate differs between papers that carry a category and papers that do not for ", flagged("first"),
         ", and the shared-author rate for ", flagged("any"), ". Differences are in percentage points.")
}

selfcat_plot <- function() {
  d <- selfcat_comparison() |>
    mutate(label = if_else(first_excludes_zero, paste0(category, " *"), category),
           row = fct_rev(fct_inorder(paste(family, category, sep = "||"))))
  lookup <- distinct(d, row, label) |> deframe()
  ggplot(d, aes(first_difference, row, colour = first_excludes_zero)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = first_lower, xmax = first_upper), size = 0.3) +
    facet_grid(family ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "firebrick", "FALSE" = "grey40"), guide = "none") +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = lookup) +
    labs(x = "Papers that carry the category minus papers that do not, in percentage points", y = NULL,
         title = "First-author self-citation rate by topic, method and source of evidence",
         subtitle = "95% intervals from resampling papers. A star marks an interval that excludes zero.") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))
}

selfcat_table <- function() {
  as_interval <- function(lower, upper) paste0(round(lower, 1), " to ", round(upper, 1))
  selfcat_comparison() |>
    transmute(Kind = as.character(family), Category = category, `Papers carrying` = papers,
              `First author, carrying (%)` = round(first_carrying, 1),
              `First author, not carrying (%)` = round(first_not_carrying, 1),
              `First author, difference (points)` = round(first_difference, 1),
              `First author, interval (points)` = as_interval(first_lower, first_upper),
              `First author, interval excludes zero` = if_else(first_excludes_zero, "yes", "no"),
              `Shared author, carrying (%)` = round(any_carrying, 1),
              `Shared author, not carrying (%)` = round(any_not_carrying, 1),
              `Shared author, difference (points)` = round(any_difference, 1),
              `Shared author, interval (points)` = as_interval(any_lower, any_upper),
              `Shared author, interval excludes zero` = if_else(any_excludes_zero, "yes", "no")) |>
    knitr::kable()
}
```

The Self-citation section of Part 2 counts the citations from each annotated paper to works that share an author with it. This section asks whether papers that carry a topic, a method or a source of evidence cite their own authors more or less than papers that do not. The first-author rate counts a citation when the citing paper's first author wrote the cited work. The shared-author rate counts it when any author of the citing paper did, and it rises with the length of the author list, so the plot uses the first-author rate and the table carries both. Each paper is a unit in the resampling that gives the 95% intervals, which are not adjusted for the number of categories compared.

### Topics, methods and sources of evidence

`r if (has_self()) selfcat_note()`

```{r}
#| label: selfcat-plot
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 14
#| eval: !expr has_self()
selfcat_plot()
```

#### Table

The numbers behind the plot: one row per category, topics first, then methods, then sources of evidence, and within each kind the category with the largest first-author difference first. "Carrying" is the share of citations that are self-citations among the papers that carry the category, and "not carrying" is the same among all other annotated papers.

```{r}
#| label: selfcat-table
#| echo: false
#| eval: !expr has_self()
selfcat_table()
```
